description.narrative:
The Project will produce a more competitive and highly skilled workforce in priority industries by developing higher level training programs at a new college level, while also establishing and strengthening system governance and quality assurance frameworks for vocational training. Studies will also strengthen the policy foundation for future development.
The project will improve the quality and management of vocational education and training (VET) programs in 15 public and 5 private vocational colleges (VCs) in economic zones offering programs for occupations in high demand in priority industries. The programs cover automotive technology, electrical manufacturing, hospitality and tourism, information and communication technology (ICT), mechanical manufacturing, and navigation and shipping. The project will consist of two loans, the first to strengthen the public vocational training system and VCs, and the second to provide private VCs with additional resources through an onlending facility. The direct beneficiaries of the project will be students in certificate and diploma vocational training courses, most of whom come from the rural lower middle class.

description.narrative: Higher-level skills training in 15 key occupations established for males and females.

85% of graduates (30% female) from 15 occupational training programs gain employment within 6 months after graduation from the VC that are targeted by SEP. Progress/Status: Baseline: 80% of 1801 graduates gained employment after graduation. Out of this, 78% [1301 graduates] gained employment within up to 3 months from graduation [20% female]. Remaining 22% gained employment after more than 3 months from graduation. Achievement: ACHIEVED. Almost 90% of graduates gained employment within 6 months after graduation Data Source: Tracer studies conducted by VCs annually.

Comprehensive national systems and plans established for college-level VET and continuously monitored for required changes by end of 2015. Progress/Status: Achieved. The national strategy for vocational training 2011-2020 was approved through Decision No. 630/QĐ-TTg dated 29/5/2012 by Prime Minister. Data Source: - National VET Strategy for the development of VCs. - National VET Training Plan developed and continuously monitored for necessary changes for college level with gender targets.

Enrollment numbers in training programs for the 15 occupations (30% females) do not exceed 125% of the established skills needs in these occupations by 2015 (baseline data to be collected at start of the project). Progress/Status: Baseline: Total enrollment in 19 VCs, 2012 = 4,013 [20% female]; 2015 = 10,177 [15% female] Achievement: Increased by 154% from 2011 to 2015 [14% female] and by 55% from 2015 to 2017 [13% female] Data Source: Aggregated VC reports, which include their annual assessment of skills needs in their respective catchment areas.

Increase to an average of 95% graduation rate in all courses for the 15 occupations by 2015 (30% of the increase in graduates to be female) from 2012 baseline. Progress/Status: Baseline: Total graduates in 19 college level schools, 2012 = 3,142; 18% female Achievement: Partly ACHIEVED the target of an increase of 20%, but not achieved the target of 30% increase of women Data Source: VC quarterly reports, with gender disaggregated data.
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: - VTIS fully developed and used by SEP's VCs by end 0f 2015. - Roll-out plan for country-wide implementation of VTIS, including budget developed and approved by MOLISA. Progress/Status: CANCELLED: The consultant completed the system design specifications in November 2011. In 2012, GDVT received financial support from MOLISA to complete an on-going development of a software. Thus, PMU proposed the cancellation of this activity in This was approved by ADB in its letter dated 20 Sep 2013. The Loan Review Mission, 1-4 Dec 2014, also noted the cancellation. Data Source: - VTIS reports on establishment and national levels, with gender disaggregated data. - Inspection of approved roll-out plan. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Gender-responsive training and learning materials and assessment tools developed for 15 occupational programs in collaboration with industry. Progress/Status: COMPLETED. Included in teacher training activities under contracts DT04 and DT05. Data Source: - Inspection of approved materials and tools and letters of endorsement from industry bodies. - Evaluation report about quality of material and assessment tools. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: National skills standards developed and issued by MOLISA by end year 2 for SEP training programs. Progress/Status: COMPLETED. National skills standards for 15 occupational programs had been issued as follows: Decision No. 1305 issued by MOT, 21 Jun 2011, for automotive technology, exploitation of marine machinery and ship control; Decision No. 4837 issued by MoIT, 22 Sep 2011, for computer network administration, computer programming, database administration, industrial electronics, electrical installation techniques and industrial control, industrial electricity, mechatronics, operation repair of refrigeration equipment and welding; Circular No. 01/2014/TT issued by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, 15 Jan 2014, for food processing and hotel management [culinary]; Decision No. 3316 issued by MIT, 14 June 2012, for metal cutting. Data Source: - MOLISA decrees or other methods of publicizing accreditations - Inspection of VTIS database that incorporates the standards. Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Pre-service training program in VCs reviewed and strengthened. Progress/Status: CANCELLED: Pre-service training activities has been canceled according to the MOU of ADB Mission on Jan 2015. Data Source: Attendance records and assessment reports, disaggregated by sex. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Professional standards for teachers and principals approved by end year 2. Progress/Status: COMPLETED: MOLISA Circular No. 08/2017/TT-BLDTBXH dated 10 March 2017 on standards for vocational teachers, which superseded Circular No. 30/2010/TT-BLDTBXH dated 29 September 2010. Data Source: Standards approved and gazetted by MOLISA. Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Program accreditation system developed and 40 programs accredited by end of Year 2 for SEP training programs. Progress/Status: Improved program accreditation system: Completed. MOLISA issued Circular No. 15/2017/TT-BLDTBXH on VT accreditation dated 8 June 2017. In line with this, PMU conducted 2 training courses.
20 programs accredited Data Source: Inspection of government gazettes or other methods of publicizing accreditations. Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Sector leadership and management strengthened through a professional development program (40% female participation). Progress/Status: COMPLETED. Three study tours [Taiwan, 15-19 July 2014; Australia, 21-25 July 2014; Malaysia 7-13 September 2014] attended by 38 participants, 21% female.
COMPLETED: Management training: Training courses for principals, vice principals and managers completed in 2016 and attended by 75 participants, 27% female. System level training courses for MOLISA, GDVT and DOLISA officers completed in 2017 and attended by 31 participants, 39% female Data Source: - Training reports - Self assessment of training participants six months after leadership training Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Quality and management of vocational training improved. Indicator: Studies on teacher incentives and new cost norms completed and recommendations agreed with government and ADB. Progress/Status: COMPLETED: Refer to Teacher Incentives Study, Final Assessment Report, January 2015 (contract TV09)
MOLISA issued Circular No. 14/2017/TT-BLDTBXH dated 25 May 2017 on technical cost norm for VT Data Source: Approved reports. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: 15 occupational training programs developed in close cooperation with the industry and approved by MOLISA by end 2012 (8 designed to attract larger numbers of female trainees). Progress/Status: Achieved. GDVT working on national standards based on ASEAN standards. Data Source: Inspection of GDVT records and publication of training programs. Target year: 2012 Target value: 15

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: 20 SEP VCs accredited by end 2012. Progress/Status: Achievement: 17 of 18 SEP VCs (94%) accredited by GDVT
Number of VCs with Level 2 accreditation by GDVT=1
Number of VCs with Level 3 accreditation by GDVT=16
Number of VCs without any GDVT accreditation=1 Data Source: GDVT accreditation records. Target year: 2012 Target value: 20

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: ERUs operational in SEP VCs with marketing plans developed by 2012 (with equal gender representation). Progress/Status: Target: 15 public VCs and 3 private VCs with operational ERU by 2012
Achievement: 2012, 7 public VCs and 1 private VC with operational ERU; by 2016, 13 public VCs and 3 private VCs. By 2016, 8 public VCs and 2 private VCs with ERUs have marketing plans Data Source: Summary marketing plans attached to VC quarterly reports. Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: Each public VC offering 1-3 SEP occupational programs by 2014. Progress/Status: Baseline: 2012 = 6 VCs offering ≥ 3 OPs, 12 VCs offering 2 OPs, and 1 VC offering 1 OP
Achievement (2016): 13 VCs offering ≥ 3 OPs, 2 VCs offering 2 OPs and none offering 1 OP. Data Source: Accreditation certificates from GDVT, MOLISA. Target year: 2014 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: Pedagogical and technical skills of vocational instructors in 20 VCs meet the standards for teaching SEP occupational programs. Progress/Status: Target: 260 teachers from 20 VCs issued teacher competency certificates by 2015
Achievement: Trained 204 teachers out of targeted 205 teachers.
Target: 500 teachers from other VCs issued teacher competency certificates by 2015
Achievement: Trained 296 teachers out of targeted 305 teachers. Data Source: Teacher competency certificates issued. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: Pilot initiatives to increase female enrollment in nontraditional areas completed. Progress/Status: Achievement: 3 out of 18 VCs (17%) have initiated work. Data Source: Report submitted by VC on each initiative. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: Planning and management skills of VC leadership improved and 20 institutional business plans developed. Progress/Status: Target: Implementation of management training package completed, 40% female participation
Achievement: Training courses for principals, vice principals and managers conducted in 3rd and 4th quarter of 2016 attended by 75 participants, 27% female.
Target: 20 institutional business plans by 2015 Achievement: Business plans were prepared by August 2017 Data Source: - VC quarterly reports - Inspection of business plans - Self-assessments six months after training event Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 2. VCs upgraded to deliver priority occupational training programs. Indicator: Skills testing centers operational at SEP VCs with 1,000 workers and 2,500 graduates (35% female) tested by 2015. Progress/Status: Target: Skills testing centers operational in 15 public VCs and 3 private VCs
Achievement: Five out of 6 skill testing centers (5 public, 1 private) are operational.
Target: 1500 workers/graduates tested by 2015, 35% female
Achievement: 1,413 workers/graduates tested by 31 August 2017 in VCs Data Source: Testing records in VC quarterly reports diaggregated by sex. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: 20% increase in revenue generated by VCs by 2015 from 2010/11 baseline. Progress/Status: Increased by 58% in 2016 Data Source: VDB quarterly reports; Summary gender plans included in VC quarterly reports; GDVT guidelines issued; SEP training program documents show on-the-job training requirements; Records of income reported by VCs in quarterly reports; MOAs signed between VCs and enterprises; Midterm and impact evaluations; and Approved report. Target year: 2015 Target value: 20

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: At least 2 formal partnership agreements a year signed between each VC and local enterprises from 2012 (at least 1 with an enterprise where most employees are female). Progress/Status: 64% of VCs with more than 2 formal partnership agreements signed per year. Three out of 18 VCs with 1 enterprise with mostly women employed Data Source: Inspection of MOAs signed between VCs and enterprises. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: Marketing plans developed for 15 SEP VCs. Progress/Status: See output 2 Data Source: Summary of marketing plan attached to VC quarterly report. Target year: 2015 Target value: 15

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: Study on how to stimulate enterprise-based training completed. Progress/Status: Enterprise-Based Training /Training Levy Study completed in Oct 2014 under contract TV08 Data Source: Approved report. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: Technical skills of 200 teachers improved through pilot training program incorporating industry training in enterprises (30% of trainee teachers to be female). Progress/Status: This activity was approved for cancellation in the Mid term review in Jan 2014. The basis of effective industry involvement in TVET is a national framework for industry to contribute to and endorse national skills standards and then a plan at the VC/province level to implement a strategy to provide cost recovery skills development to industry based on the industry approved standards. Each target VC requires and operational plan including a marketing strategy targeting industry and communities in its own province. Funds are no longer required in either teacher training or management training for this activity. Consultants engaged will concentrate on strengthening each target VC in this area to improve the responsiveness of VCs to the demand for training and the need for non-government based revenue. Data Source: - Training reports - Self assessment of training participants 6 months after training events. - SEP training program documents show on-the-job training requirements. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: Training programs in the 15 occupations are developed in close consultations with industries, in whcih the occupations typically occur. Progress/Status: Activities for this sub component have been integrated into other subcomponents Data Source: Survey of enterprises involved in developig training programs. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: VCs borrowing from onlending facility expand enrollments by 20% (20% of the increase to be female) in occupations targeted by SEP. Progress/Status: Only 3 subloans approved: 1. Bac Nam VC: subloan includes construction of multi-function workshop, supply of vocational equipment and supply and installation of equipment for fire protection and firefighting. Post-review of Bac Nam VC bidding documents for the construction of multifunctional building has been approved in July 2014. Bidding documents for supply of vocational equipment submitted for post review. VC has fully utilized the subloan.
2. An Nhat Vinh VC: subloan includes construction, expansion and improvement (including supply and installation of equipment/furniture). Post-review of An Nhat Vinh VC NCB documents for its construction, expansion, and improvement has been approved in June 2014. Civil works component completed but large packages of equipment not procured due to change in equipment list.
3. Dong An VC: subloan includes construction and purchase of equipment. Civil works completed but procurement of equipment not completed.
Total enrollment in 3 private VCs, 2011-12 = 1471 (55% female). In 2016, enrollment increased by 36%, 43% female Data Source: - VDB quarterly reports - Summary gender plans included in VC quarterly report - GDVT guidelines issued - Records of income reported by VCs in quarterly reports. Target year: 2015 Target value: 20

Output: 3. Partnerships with the private sector strengthened. Indicator: VCs borrowing from onlending facility have an institution-specific gender strategy. Progress/Status: NOT ACHIEVED. No private VC-participant with an institution-specific gender strategy Data Source: - VDB quarterly reports - Summary gender plans included in VC quarterly report - GDVT guidelines issued - Records of income reported by VCs in quarterly reports. Target year: 2015 Target value: Y
